items.title: Bill Crow interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, October 18, 1995
items.q: And then I’d run down the street to Jack Silver’s Tuxedo Shop and rent a jacket or a tux for another $5.

ctx.x: Greenwell, wonderful tenor player who had been living in Seattle for a long time; and a trumpet player named Marty Bell, who is still around in Florida someplace; and a piano player named John Vincent Brooks, who had been the arranger for Randy Brooks’ band when Buzzy was on that band. Buzzy Bridgeford was his name. And he couldn’t hire a bass player, the boss wouldn’t go for another rhythm instrument. So he goes back up with this quartet, and he tells me when he leaves, he said “look, we’re going to be up there…

Wolfe’s String Shop and rent an old beat up bass that he had there. He would charge $5 for the weekend. And then I’d run down the street to Jack Silver’s Tuxedo Shop and rent a jacket or a tux for another $5. And the job paid $15, on which the profit of $5 I could live for a week you know?
